key_insight: Across 30 LLMs, strong diagnostic performance did not translate into reliable downstream cancer care, and dominant error types shifted by care phase.
clinical_relevance: Evaluating medical AI across the full care pathway may reveal omissions and decision errors missed by diagnosis-only benchmarks.
method: Built NPC-RubricBench from longitudinal nasopharyngeal carcinoma records at two cancer centers.
Evaluated 30 general-purpose and medical LLMs across six care phases using patient-specific criteria and decision-time evidence only.
Compared broad requests with detailed, checklist-like prompts.
evidence_signal: The benchmark included 405 patients, 941 patient-phase units, and 17,688 criteria; explicit decision errors dominated anatomical staging (48.2%), while omissions dominated initial work-up (33.4%) and post-treatment follow-up (30.4%).
watch_item: Detailed prompts improved Decision Quality but reduced Evidence Faithfulness and Safety Adherence, highlighting a trade-off that requires validation before clinical deployment.
paper_title: Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
